# MarkItDown backlog closure review

Snapshot: September 6, 2026. Reviewed all **316 open issues and 315 open PRs (631 total)** in the captured inventory.

Code baseline: [main at 4459ed0](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/commit/4459ed01155f8e1a7ac007f441d34f0422746191) (September 4, 2026). Latest stable release: v0.1.7; latest prerelease: v0.1.8b1. A fix on main is not necessarily in the stable release.

No issues or PRs were closed, edited, commented on, or otherwise modified.

This is a self-contained snapshot for later maintenance work. All 631 item assessments, evidence, recommended actions, and consolidation notes are included below.

## Paste-ready closing messages: already addressed PRs

Drafts for the 17 PRs grouped as "Already addressed by accepted changes" in the summary. Copy the fenced text into the corresponding PR. Each message links to the merged PR or PRs that address its proposed change. These drafts have not been posted.

### PR #295 - DOCX math formulas

```markdown
Thank you for working on DOCX equation support. The core OMML-to-LaTeX conversion was implemented in [#1160](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/1160), including inline and block equations, and is now part of the existing DOCX conversion path.

I'm closing this alternative implementation as superseded. Specific equations that still fail or render incorrectly can be tracked separately with a small example document against the current implementation.
```

### PR #1172 - Quoting README installation commands

```markdown
Thanks for catching the shell-quoting problem. Both installation-command corrections proposed here were incorporated in [#1175](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/1175): the source-install command and the selective-extras example now quote the package argument.

Closing this as already addressed; thank you for the contribution.
```

### PR #1215 - CSV converter

```markdown
Thank you for proposing CSV-to-Markdown support. A CSV converter was implemented and registered in [#1176](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/1176), so CSV files already use the built-in conversion pipeline.

I'm closing this separate converter implementation as superseded. Any remaining CSV parsing or rendering edge cases should be reported against the existing converter.
```

### PR #1417 - Missing DOCX style identifiers

```markdown
Thanks for investigating the DOCX style-metadata crash. [#2190](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/2190) addresses it during preprocessing: styles without w:styleId are removed and missing w:type values are supplied before the document reaches Mammoth.

Closing this as superseded by that fix. It is included in main and the v0.1.8b1 prerelease, but not v0.1.7. If the same failure occurs with the updated implementation, a minimal DOCX reproducer would help us track the remaining case.
```

### PR #1465 - ONNX Runtime dependency constraint

```markdown
Thank you for looking into the ONNX Runtime constraint. We addressed the direct dependency pin in [#1551](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/1551) by removing MarkItDown's onnxruntime<=1.20.1 entry entirely, rather than retaining the cap and applying it to additional platforms.

I'm closing this as superseded by that change. This only resolves the direct-pin change proposed here; broader Python/platform compatibility and transitive dependency constraints remain separate concerns.
```

### PR #1494 - UTF-8 output-file reading in CLI tests

```markdown
Thanks for identifying the locale-dependent decoding failure in test_output_to_file. [#2351](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/2351) incorporated the same correction: the test now reads the generated output with an explicit UTF-8 encoding.

The change is on main, so I'm closing this PR as already addressed. Thank you for contributing the fix.
```

### PR #1538 - Multiline CSV cells breaking Markdown tables

```markdown
Thank you for the multiline-CSV example and proposed fix. [#2266](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/2266) addresses the reported table breakage by escaping Markdown-sensitive cell content and replacing embedded line breaks with spaces in both headers and data cells.

This preserves table integrity while keeping CSV conversion independent of pandas. It does not preserve visual multiline layout within a cell. The fix is in main and v0.1.8b1, so I'm closing this parser-replacement proposal as superseded.
```

## How to use this report

- **Close** means the available discussion, diff, current source, or merged history supports closure now. It is a recommendation, not an action already taken.
- **Conditional** is not an automatic closure list. Preserve a canonical issue/implementation, make the stated policy decision, or request the specified information before closing.
- **Keep** includes genuine unresolved work and items where evidence does not support closure. It does not imply that a PR is merge-ready.
- Age, conflicts, failing checks, brief descriptions, non-English writing, and apparent AI authorship are not sufficient closure grounds.
- Duplicate proposals are grouped for consolidation without assuming an unmerged PR has solved the underlying issue. A linked canonical item is a tracking target, not necessarily an endorsed implementation.

## Method and limitations

Every inventory item received a recorded disposition. Reviews used full issue bodies/discussions, PR file patches and review/conversation information, current source, all 237 merged PRs, and indexes of closed issues/PRs. Decisive history and references were followed as needed. This is a static maintenance triage, not execution of untrusted PR code, exhaustive reproduction of every reported bug, or a security audit. Per-item limitations are recorded below. GitHub is live, so status should be rechecked immediately before acting.

A final inventory refresh found the same 631 open items with no changed update timestamps. Large generated assets, binary fixtures, repetitive mappings, and long documentation/style sections were reviewed structurally where noted, rather than claiming line-by-line review of every byte.

## Important distinctions

- No item is recommended for closure solely as spam. [#2386](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/issues/2386) is an intentional maintainer-hosted experiment. [#1843](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/1843) contains project documentation despite its title; its closure follows the explicit English-only repository-documentation policy, not an inference of spam. Other submissions contain unrelated material or objectively nonfunctional changes, identified specifically rather than attributed to authorship.
- [#2033](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/2033) warrants separate private credential hygiene follow-up: its added documents contain apparent provider credentials. Values were neither reproduced in this report nor tested. Closing a PR does not remove credentials from its history.
- PDF structure and OCR are not generally solved. Preserve concrete regressions such as [#120](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/issues/120), [#213](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/issues/213), [#293](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/issues/293), [#1117](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/issues/1117), [#1419](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/issues/1419), [#1791](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/issues/1791), [#2343](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/issues/2343), [#2382](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/issues/2382), [#2383](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/issues/2383). Closure of broad delivered-capability questions does not imply these edge cases work.
- [#2360](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/2360) increases charset sampling to 64 KiB; it is not a whole-file decoding fallback. [#2371](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/2371) fixes notebook heading-prefix handling, not [#2115](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/issues/2115)'s string-source bug.
- [#1897](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/issues/1897) still tracks advertised OCR CLI flags that do not exist. Recommendations involving the OCR plugin use its separately installed, explicitly configured Python integration.
- [#1905](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/issues/1905) and [#1927](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/1927) require a trust-boundary decision; this report does not declare the existing security concern fixed or dismiss hosted deployments.

## Consolidation guide

These are **choices between still-open implementations**, not evidence that a feature has shipped. Preserve unique behavior and fixtures before closing alternatives. The per-item report distinguishes genuinely redundant patches from proposals that need substantial repair.

| Family | Tracker / implementation choices | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| Legacy DOC | Issue #23; PRs #1252, #1316, #1616, #1624, #1710, #1869, #2013, #2058, #2100, #2244, #2256 | Choose plugin/core ownership and one backend first. System-tool, COM and pure-Python approaches have different tradeoffs. Nonfunctional #1598 and #2270 are separately recommended closures, not canonical implementations. |
| EML | Issues #89 and #1662; PRs #1503, #1633, #1663, #1877, #1890, #1926, #2206 | Select one header/body/attachment contract. #1663 is a useful attachment-capable comparison point; #1926 also bundles unrelated Word/PPTX changes. |
| XLSX display formatting | Issue #53; PRs #1325, #1630, #1878, #1944, #2005, #2149, #2347 | Set the number-format fidelity/configuration contract, then consolidate. A currency-only formatter is not equivalent to comprehensive Excel display formatting. |
| Decoding fallback | PRs #1540, #1938, #1954, #1956, #1964, #2015, #2280, #2337, #2346 | Coordinate plaintext and CSV recovery. Keep coverage for incorrect explicit charset hints and non-ASCII data after 64 KiB; merged #2360 does not cover these. |
| TSV | Issue #2022; PRs #2021, #2027, #2061 | #2027 is the narrow explicit TSV route. Choose whether delimiter inference is desired before retaining the broader alternatives. |
| Document Intelligence features | Issues #1536 and #2273; PRs #1561, #1595, #1647, #1913, #1959, #1975, #2284 | Separate default FORMULAS policy from custom model/query/feature APIs. Select one default-policy patch and retain independently useful configuration work. |
| API-key documentation | Issue #1446; PRs #1559, #1603, #1634, #1695 | Authentication code already exists, but the README example gap remains. Consolidate the overlapping documentation without calling the gap implemented. |
| UTF-8 stdout | PRs #1586, #1656, #1790, #1864, #1966, #2175 | Distinguish avoiding an exception through replacement characters from lossless redirected UTF-8. Salvage independent Windows test improvements rather than closing entire bundles as fixed. |
| Page/source provenance | Issue #122; PRs #1263, #1375, #2272 | Structured page results, textual page markers, and spreadsheet row anchors are related but not identical. Agree a coherent API/output contract. |
| Batch conversion | Issue #1371; PRs #1372, #1793, #1825, #2353 | Choose a shared API/CLI design. The standalone script is not automatically out of scope, but should not create a competing CLI surface without need. |
| MCP file output | Issue #1332; PRs #1360, #2202 | Choose one file/resource response design and preserve context-budget requirements before closing the other implementation. |
| HTTP timeouts | Issue #1167; PRs #1412, #1999 | Choose configurable timeout semantics rather than accepting multiple incompatible defaults. Issue #2000 can close as a duplicate now. |
| ZIP limits | Issue #1514; PRs #1628, #1666, #2050, #2296 | Agree archive limit configuration and failure behavior. #2296 also touches URL/resource limits, so it is not wholly interchangeable with ZIP-only work. |
| YouTube/Python dependency updates | Issue #2287; PRs #1683, #1732, #2077, #2179 | Separate the incompatible all-extra constraint from broader Python/platform support. The API-breaking #2339 is a closure candidate, not a replacement. |
| Scanned/mixed-page OCR | Issues #1791 and #2343; PRs #1888, #1920, #1933, #2276, #2348 | Keep one coherent fix path covering page-marker emptiness, mixed documents, crop bounds and ordering. Do not treat the existing OCR package as proof these failures are solved. |
| DOCX internal anchors | Issue #314; PRs #2131, #2265 | Choose consistent internal-link semantics; preserve the newer #2125 reproducer when closing that duplicate issue. |
| Native/non-OpenAI clients | Issue #1129; PRs #265, #1449, #1475 | Distinguish OpenAI-compatible endpoint configuration from native SDK adapters and provider discovery. Close the mixed web-app #257 independently of this valid capability. |

The full report identifies dozens of PRs as conditional duplicates. This guide also includes retained comparison candidates, so its rows must not be interpreted as a list of PRs to close en masse.
